items.title: Just listen.
items.your_version: “How do I do this?” you ask. Just listen silently. Many people skip the listening or shorten it since it's not "achieving something" but this is by far the most important step. When you warm up to what’s there, protect it, clarify what it is, reality test it, and then act on it, you’ll find that you don’t even need to have a dramatic trance experience to demonstrate the results of all parts of your mind talking to each other and trusting each other more.

items.title: The body's no
items.where: Why doing it myself worked better for me, P2
items.my_version: When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using for a suggestion to my subconscious is slightly off, and talk to my subconscious to find out what it thinks is wrong with the wording. When I use an image, I can tell whether it's giving me useful information, or just telling me what I'm afraid of, or what I want to avoid, or what I want to be true, or something I don't understand yet. I can tell when my body is saying no, before my conscious mind can twist it around to a yes.

items.title: One person, three jobs
items.where: The inner child, the guards, and the inner adult’s three jobs, P2
items.my_version: Here I’m going to talk about what you develop in yourself as you reparent your inner child. It’s one person doing three jobs rather than getting three more people to move in with you to help with the rent! Each job keeps the others in balance. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.

items.title: I still love you.
items.where: Love doesn’t have to wait for trust, P2
items.my_version: You could say something like, "Okay. I believe that you don't believe me. I still love you. You don't have to love me back. Tell me what feels unsafe." items.title: What did it understand back then? What options c...
items.my_version: When you're placing your younger self on trial, instead of asking which age of you deserves the blame, ask: What was that age of you trying to get, or get away from? What did it understand back then? What options could it actually see? Could it stand to take any of them? What happened because of the choice it made? What was missing? Some ability, or help/protection from someone else? What can you learn or repair now, and how would you act differently in such situations? Even if what it did was harmful to you and others, punishing yourself now is not going to give it the capacity it needed at the time.

items.title: Tired?
items.my_version: If it's hard to bring up the warm stuff, you can always do something to protect your inner child. Make sure they're small enough that you can actually do them. If you're not able to, figure out what's getting in the way of you doing them. Are you scared? Tired? Do you not know how to? Is there a practical thing that's getting in your way? Have you set yourself up to do it in a way that's likely to be successful? Don't make it so that doing it successfully means you have to feel good about it, or be able to check it off a list.

items.title: etc.
items.my_version: Ask them for help with directing your life. The Guide holds standards, the way a good parent would, and asks hard things of your inner child so it can grow, at its own pace. Your parent’s harsh tone doesn’t come with the job, though, so be careful not to ask for the kind of “tough it out, you don’t have needs, you just need discipline!” kind of direction. Without the Guide, you can also slide from looking after your inner child into spoiling it: sweets and screens can pass for loving yourself, and so can getting it out of anything hard. Ask them for help in directing you to do adult things in a way that takes your needs into account: asking for the help you need, expressing your preferences, letting a safe person see you in an imperfect way, finding ways to get your need for closeness met without punishing someone for their need for space, etc. etc.

items.title: What the parent script is
items.my_version: One important thing to become aware of when approaching your inner child is your inherited parent script. Your parent script is made up of a collection of rules and ways of treating yourself that you adopted as a child (mostly based on how you were treated by your parent(s)). It doesn’t always take the form of a voice. This is not the inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Guide) that you consciously build. Often this script acts as a critic or warden, telling your inner child not to cry, not to be “needy”, not to embarrass them, not to be too independent, etc. So when you begin talking to your child in a new, loving way, the script may jump in to say that what you’re doing is “fake”.

items.title: Temporary Separation.
items.where: When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice, P11
items.my_version: Temporary Separation. Sometimes it may be wise to remove yourself, for a time, from the people or group that you normally would get answers from. Some people come back later on different terms, and sometimes the break has to be long-term because the pattern of losing yourself with them is deeply entrenched. As you differentiate, you learn to tell which of those apply. You want to let your quieter preferences bubble up to the surface so you can be sure you’re not just echoing your social group.

items.title: Part of that might be deepening.
items.where: What an induction is actually doing, P1
items.my_version: Getting yourself ready to do something. Part of that is gathering your attention up. Part of that might be deepening. Part of that is letting what you notice inform the words you're hearing and what you do next. There are lots of different ways to do this. For this method, I'm going to be counting, but you could do all sorts of things. If you want to just talk, or tell a story, or move, or make sounds, or be curious, or whatever, by all means, just do that. The only thing is, say that you're doing it. Don't pretend you're doing something else, in the name of elegance or whatever.

One thing you're doing, one anchor/image you're going with at first, one way of coming back, and feel free to set a tone (warm, bounded, directed, neutral witnessing, whatever) for yourself. If you're going to use metaphors just do one, and if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that's conscious.

items.title: Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional...
items.where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P2
items.my_version: Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional. You can use whatever form of signal makes sense to you (feelings, rhythms, movements, words, spatial, simple knowing, lack of signal, whatever) but if you're using words, try to keep them related to whatever world you're creating. If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world. And when you're done, come back the other way. (You can borrow qualities, but don't change who you are.)

items.title: Read it out loud
items.where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P3
items.my_version: When you're writing this, think about what the verb you're using is, what the sensory quality is, what the short refrain is, and how you're going to transition between ideas. items.title: What you want to do today
items.my_version: Think about what you want to do. Are there things you don’t want to do today? How long do you want to spend on this? (You don't have to do this on a problem. You can do it on something you want to experience more of: love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, whatever.) Make sure you're leaving some time at the end to come back, and reflect on what you experienced.

items.title: The three stop words
items.my_version: Deciding to do it. How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? Something else? Preview what you are going to do: will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can. Remind yourself that if you say 'stop' at any time, the induction will end. If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less. If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop. You can also just open your eyes and stop, and then come all the way back anyway. You don't need to ask any parts for permission to stop, even if a part tells you that you do.

items.title: Utilize.
items.my_version: Let your response guide you as to what to do next regardless of what the script is expecting. Utilize. Use what you have to go to the next place, whatever it is. Learn how to notice what is there. Learn how to notice if there is no change, and that no change is not a positive change. For more on language you can use, see Appendix B, or keep reading below for information on using the tools after induction in Let the next response guide you. Either way, keep the instructions about how to stay safe and how to get out plain.

items.title: Orient yourself by looking around. Where are you...
items.where: Already open? Contain before you deepen, P3
items.my_version:
Orient yourself by looking around. Where are you? What's the date or day? How does your body feel? Where are you grounded? Can you feel your feet/hands/spine/etc? Make some contact with yourself, eg press your thumbs against the tips of your index fingers gently but firmly so that you can feel friction. Focus on that.

Say something like, "Only what I can integrate, please. If there's too much it can wait. My body may stay safe. I'll be here as an adult, this won't just be my inner child."

When you feel oriented, make an intention.

items.title: Just notice, keep yourself up straight and work...

items.my_version: “Starting with your eyes open press your thumb to your forefinger. And as you press your fingers together gently and release, you begin to bring yourself into a place of clearer awareness… again you press your fingers together and release, bringing yourself into an even clearer state of awareness. Just notice, keep yourself up straight and work at this level.

items.title: Don’t use this to go into hypnosis faster for th...
items.where: A shortcut back into hypnosis, P6
items.my_version:
Also, be sure that this is working for you. Be able to turn it on and off at will. Make sure it isn't there when you don't want it to be. Be able to change directions or come back up when you are in it. Don't use it in a way that makes you follow instructions that you are hearing from a narrator, notifications, or something that you overhear. Don't use this to go into hypnosis faster for things that you shouldn't be working on yet.

There is something you should never do while using this induction. And that's use it, practice it or test it while you're driving or doing something where you need to be actively paying attention. It's just not safe to be going into a trance where you are actively paying attention to what's going on inside of you when you need to be paying attention to what's going on outside of you. Even though your eyes can be open, even though you're using "if it would be useful for you to do so" type language, it's just not safe.

items.title: Etcetera.
items.where: Come all the way back, P1
items.my_version: If you have done anything to alter your state when entering the trance, make sure to reverse those things. If you have floated, make sure to gain your weight again (whatever weight you want of course). If you have shrunk, make sure to grow back to your regular size. If you have met a younger state or are working with parts, make sure to come back to feeling complete in your body in the here and now, that your body belongs to you, and that it is under the control of your adult mind. If you have gone somewhere, make sure to go back the same way you went there. Etcetera.

items.title: The only intention I will take with me into my e...
items.where: Come all the way back, P2
items.my_version: Here is a generic bring-back that you can use: "When I come out of this session, I will only bring with me that which is useful to me in my everyday life right now. Anything else I will bring with me at a later date, when I am better able to integrate it. When I come out of this session, I will be coming back to the room I am in now, and to the day in which I am participating in this session now. All the instructions you have given me to carry me deeper into this session or keep me in this state are now finished. The only intention I will take with me into my everyday life, and the only cue I will use to take me into this state at a later date, will be the ones I consciously choose, and neither of them will keep me in this state. When I come out of this session I will be me, in my body and with my adult judgment."

items.title: On 2 start to feel your breathing return to norm...
items.where: Come all the way back, P3
items.my_version: Then do a count up: On 1 start to feel your body again and what it's resting on and feel your weight (of your choice). On 2 start to feel your breathing return to normal. On 3 start to hear the room around you and name where you are. On 4 start to wiggle your fingers and toes, move your shoulders and your eyes. On 5 open your eyes, back in the here and now, feeling normal and clear and the session is now over.

items.title: Move around a bit.
items.where: Come all the way back, P4
items.my_version: When you come out make sure you can name what day (or date) it is, look to your left and right, look at something near to you and something further away. Move around a bit. Don't get up until you feel like you can do so without falling over. Make sure that you are oriented and alert (counting does this, but not always). Take mental note of only what actually came up for you and any actions you need to take regarding it. Then go on and do something normal.

items.title: Then just listen.
items.my_version: Then just listen. You don't need fancy language - often it will be better to just ask what happens next, or whatever. If you notice a feeling developing, it might be best not to say anything while it's developing (if you can help it) but some days you need to talk to understand, so just do that.

items.title: One next action
items.my_version: “Dear Wise Subconscious Mind, if there is something you know that my conscious self is not ready to know, please don’t break it open violently! Do what you can to make me able to know it in a way that is safe! Prepare me BEFORE you break it open! Ground me BEFORE you show me the memory! Support me BEFORE you make it intense! What is one next thing I can do?” etc.

items.title: Treat it as an image
items.my_version: REMEMBER: Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal, especially if it has to do with trauma or memories. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So take it as an image and get some outside help!

items.title: The smaller asks
items.my_version: Maybe ask to be shown just one body sensation, or just one word. Or even just whether today is for listening or resting.

items.title: What feels fake
items.my_version: Have you got any sense of what it is that's making it feel fake? The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc. It doesn't matter that you don't have an inner voice/image to do this, it isn't necessarily about not having a 'grown up' or resisting doing the work. If it feels like you are being asked to do something you don't want to do then correct this. It could be that there is a part that is protecting you, so talk to it.

items.title: The part that remembers
items.my_version: You could say something like 'What are you protecting me from?' or 'Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?' or 'Are you afraid this will just be a performance?' If it says yes, that one can sting, because there could be something to it. You may have fooled yourself in the past, and that part remembers. "Tell me what you remember, I'm listening." works well here.

items.title: Big or hard-to-undo things wait

It should make sense to you and if it's something big or hard to undo, wait till you're calm and then check it out with what you know.

items.title: I don’t have to obey it. I don’t even have to at...
items.where: Appendix C: The extended de-hypnosis checklist, P1
items.my_version: What to do when you feel like you’re being pushed too hard by something (person, ad, ideology, spiritual teaching, romantic attraction, internal voice, etc.): Say to yourself, “Okay, something is trying to influence me here. I don’t have to obey it. I don’t even have to attack it. I can just slow myself down and ask some questions like, 'What would this thing influence me to believe that isn’t true in order to get what it wants from me? What is my body telling me to do about this (how does my body feel)? What would love do here? What would truth do here? How would I approach this humbly? What would life have me do here?'”

items.title: The hypnosis-specific audit
items.my_version:
Before accepting a recording or live suggestion, ask:

Was I plainly told that induction mechanics are being used?

Can at least one answer lead to pause, modification, full alertness, or stopping?

Does the speaker treat not noticing as secret proof that the process worked?

Are roles, ownership, obedience, age, identity, or belonging being used to lower adult judgment?

Are fractionation, cues, later behavior, or memory effects disclosed before they are used?

Are ordinary body sensations being turned into evidence for a hidden claim?

Does the exit restore ordinary identity, movement, orientation, and critical judgment—and plainly say that the session has ended?

When an answer is unclear, stay fully alert. Ask for the exact script, change the method, or leave.

items.title: You learn to track.
items.my_version: Somatic experiencing: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide. In somatic experiencing (SE), you are not thrusting into the trauma. You learn to track. So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.

items.title: Work with the body.
items.my_version: Work with the body. Sometimes the mind is too activated for meditation to help, so you may need to work directly with the body to calm it down. Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc. (Avoid massaging the front of the neck. Also avoid massaging injured or numb body parts, or bruised, inflamed, or recently surgically operated on areas, or varicose veins. Also stop if the massage makes the anxiety symptoms worse, or makes you feel bad in any way, such as painful, dizzy, tingly, etc.) There are many other somatic approaches you can try, like heat, pressure, a weighted blanket, darkness, your favorite calming music, a careful use of a massage gun, etc.

items.title: Here is some inner child love.
items.my_version: Here is some inner child love. Put your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexus, and say to yourself in a loving way, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix it. I’m here now, and the adult is here now to listen to you.” Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death. No warmth today? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.

items.title: Finding my body parts
items.my_version: Let’s see if I can find my body parts. What are my feet doing? How is my body positioned in the chair? How is my body breathing? How is my body situated in the room?

items.title: If you’re dealing with particularly complicated...
items.where: Appendix F: Self-trust, outside guidance, and oracle-like states, P3
items.my_version: That said, self hypnosis may be the best way of talking to your subconscious on a day to day basis. If you’re dealing with particularly complicated trauma, blind spots, dissociation, destabilization, or relational wounds that need another nervous system, skilled outside support may be best.

items.title: I won’t use spirituality to silence your pain.
items.my_version: “You don’t have to forgive before you’re ready. I won’t use spirituality to silence your pain. And I won’t build our whole life around this wound forever.”
items.before: “You don’t have to forgive before you’re ready. I won’t use spirituality to silence your pain. And I won’t build our whole life around this wound forever.”

items.title: What does accountability require?
items.my_version: What actually happened? What was the impact? What boundaries need to be set? What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm? What is theirs? What is mine? What does accountability require? How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?

items.title: Borrowing Nurturer and Protector
items.my_version: This is NOT to say that you SHOULD use substances, but many people have used them when they first did self-hypnosis, contacted their inner child, or talked to their Higher Self. I’d learn the inner child work sober first, with enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep (see the inner child reparenting section). Borrow some from someone else if you need to, but make sure they're stable and not someone who will try to direct your trip.

items.title: Hear it out first.)
items.my_version: A lot of people have OPENED themselves up to something at one point in their life. If you've had a similar experience, know that there is a difference between having experienced it at one point, or only being able to access it in a certain state, and being able to get to it at any point in your life. Let that experience inform what you OPEN yourself up to. (If you can't give it to the child, try to deal with why you can't, instead of trying to ramp up the experience. Often it’s a protective part that’s seen love come with strings before. Hear it out first.)

items.title: The test for a response
items.where: A response check, not a verdict about what it is, P4
items.my_version: You don’t have to find out if it’s a guard immediately, and you may not be able to comfort it quickly. Is this way of responding helping you to be clearer and steadier and less hooked?
